messages.subject: Running Monthly Analysis for Multiple Years, Snowpack
messages.subject_clean: Running Monthly Analysis for Multiple Years, Snowpack
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I’m trying to run an analysis using monthly climate data to simulate snowpack. However, I can’t seem to figure out how to get the microclimate model to run for multiple years. I’ve been trying to follow the vignettes on the NicheMapR website (like this one https://mrke.github.io/NicheMapR/inst/doc/microclimate-IO), and I can get the model to run fine for one year, but I need to run the model for longer such that the annual cycles stabilize. It seems like this is super straightforward when using the other microclimate functions (micro_global, micro_usa, etc.) as they have a parameter built in to change the number of years (nyears), but I haven’t found an analogous method for extending the run time in the customizable microclimate model.

So my question is this: is it possible to run the microclimate model at a monthly resolution, using my own forcing data, for multiple years?

Hope my question is clear!

Ryan

messages.subject: Re: Running Monthly Analysis for Multiple Years, Snowpack
messages.subject_clean: Running Monthly Analysis for Multiple Years, Snowpack
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ryan,

You will just need to repeat all the time-dependent input data for however many years you want to do. If you look at the code for micro_global, and search for 'nyears' you'll see how that's done and you should be able to insert similar code into your custom function. Hope that helps.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: micro_era5 and micro_ncep change
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mike,

I have some questions about the rainhourly vector that you can input in the microclimate model (using micro_ncep function).
I am running the micro_ncep function on repeated locations but it seems that depending on the coordinates, for same dates and rainfall input, the snowdepth is not always well modelled (production of NaN in the metout output).

If the 'rainhour' vector is provided (with rainhourly = 1) and is only a vector of hourly rainfall values, how does the model knows exactly at which dates the vector is starting and ending?
Did you test this parameter running micro_ncep function on multiple years and modelling snowfalls and snowdepths?

I also tried inputing daily rainfall values (with dailyprecip), which works well on the different coordinates.

I don't know if someone else has tried the rainhour parameter and managed to get it work?
I am using the 3.2.1 NicheMapR version.

Thank you very much!
Anouch T

Le mardi 2 août 2022 à 14:59:36 UTC+2, NicheMapR a écrit :
> Also when I made this change initially, I forgot about some subsequent code that caused a rather big problem (hourly rain vector became one value, zero!). I fixed that problem this morning so I think it's all working properly now.
>
> On Monday, July 25, 2022 at 5:24:04 PM UTC+10 NicheMapR wrote:
> > Hi everyone,
> > I wanted to alert you to a change I've made to micro_era5 and micro_ncep to prevent them from getting stuck in endless loops in some circumstances. The short story is it won't make any difference to your calculations other than preventing the endless loops.
> >
> > The longer story is that I found that in some places the integrator was having difficulty finding a solution on days with a relatively large daily precipitation. In the microclimate model, the precipitation meant to fall daily at midnight. However, because the input data for micro_ncep and micro_era5 can start at times other than midnight, depending on the timezone (because it is based on UTC), there were situations where the precipitation was falling when there was high solar radiation. I've fixed it by putting the daily rainfall into the hourly rainfall input vector, on the hours that are local solar midnight.
> >
> > Hope that makes sense. The change is presently only on the github version.
> >
> > All the best,
> > Mike

However, I still have the problem, that I don't understand: it is modelling well on some points and not until the end on others, which are really close spatially and with the same specified options. For example, on GPS coordinates (-114.6668, 50.63571), it models the right snow depth over the entire period, but on coordinates (-114.6661, 50.63590) it stops modelling after the 30 April 2019 (any variable).

I also checked, and there is no interruption in our precipitation vector.

And this is happening only with hourly precipitations in input (and not when running the model alone or with daily precipitations).
Do you have any idea of why such problem can happen?

Thank you very much,
Anouch

messages.subject: Calculating back feed requirements based on pA
messages.subject_clean: Calculating back feed requirements based on pA
messages.body_plain:
Dear Mike,

I'm using NicheMapR to get growth and feed requirement estimates in the context of fish farming using parameters taken from Add my pet.

In the context of fish farming, the animals are often assumed fed add libitum so we run the model with a non-limiting X (simulating f=1) but adapting temperature to realistic time series.

We do obtain realistic growth estimates.

To back-calculate the feed requirements, we sum pA values for each time step during the whole farming period and divide this value by the digestible energy density in the food (kJ/g DM). The digestible energy density value is often communicated by feed manufacturers and was checked for consistency. I don't understand why this calculation results in abnormally low feed requirements.

We also accounted for the conversion Dry weight -> wet weight of the feed, so the inconsistency doesn't come from that.

Would you have an idea of the origin of the problem?

Best,
Killian

messages.subject: Tide parameters in microclimate
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
Now I want to use NichemapR-microclimate to predict intertidal microenvironmental data. This requires the input parameter Tides. But the Tides given in the document seems to have no practical significance.

# intertidal simulation input vector (col 1 = tide in(1)/out(0), col 2 = sea water temperature in °C, col 3 = % wet from wave splash)
tides <- matrix(data = 0, nrow = 24 * doynum, ncol = 3) # matrix for tides

And I'm not sure about the format of col1 and col3 and how they will be entered.

Thank You.

messages.subject: Re: Tide parameters in microclimate
messages.body_plain:
Hi - the tides simulation is not well tested so it will be worth having some real data to assess how well it works. It tries to capture the effect of water coming in over the substrate by simulating a very strong convective connection to the water temperature by making the wind speed arbitrarily high (50000 m/s!) and having only convection and conduction involved in the heat budget when the tide is in.

When you say the tides given in the document have no practical significance, I presume you're referring to the fact that by default an empty matrix is passed. That is to prevent a tidal simulation from occurring by default. As the instructions say though, you just make a matrix where the first column consists of 1 or 0 indicating whether the tide is in or out that hour, column 2 is the sea water temperature in deg C, and column 3 is a number that indicates the percentage wetness of the surface if you want to simulate a situation where waves are splashing the site of interest.

Does that help?

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Tide parameters in microclimate
messages.body_plain:
If you want a true tide model, you could consider xtide (https://flaterco.com/).  This program comes with tidal constituents for a reasonably large number of sites around the world.  The command-line tool  xtide in the package can be run with a system() call in R.  If you are working in the USA, the rtide package can be useful - it has constituents from NOAA.

You can get seawater temperature from one of the L4 (cloud-free) datasets like the UK MetOffice global daily 5km scale SST, available from marine.copernicus.eu <http://marine.copernicus.eu> (product  SST_GLO_SST_L4_NRT_OBSERVATIONS_010_001 ) or from  podaac.jpl.nasa.gov <http://podaac.jpl.nasa.gov>
(product  OSTIA-UKMO-L4-GLOB-v2.0).  The near real-time product covers the period 2007-present, and the reanalysis product (available only from marine.copernicus.eu <http://marine.copernicus.eu>) covers the period back to 1982.  An alternative is the CCI-SST which is a carefully curated, de-biased, and homogenized L4 5km global daily cloud free SST climate data record from the European Space Agency: https://climate.esa.int/en/projects/sea-surface-temperature/ 1982-present. Higher spatial resolution products exist for shorter time periods and smaller geographic regions.  See the GHRSST product collection at PODAAC.

David Wethey

messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I am new to ecological models in R, and am looking to use NicheMapR
to assess how different climate temperature scenarios affect the blue mussel
Mytilus edulis.

I was wondering whether there is a tutorial for the “Dynamic
energy budget model in the sea” shiny app, and whether this could be done in R?

I was also wondering whether there’s a manual for the
NicheMapR package and some information surrounding the parameters, as I have
tried to run the basic deb model using the Mytilus edulis data from A.M.P, and
have had some problems with the parameters (It ran fine with Mytilus trossulus
data)

Thanks in advance for your time!

Fabian
